newsitem.title: BERMUDA: NZ SPORT - New coaches for Chiefs and Highlanders.
newsitem.headline: NZ SPORT - New coaches for Chiefs and Highlanders.

text.p: HAMILTON, Aug 19 - All Black selector Ross Cooper and unfancied Tony Gilbert were on Tuesday named coaches for the Waikato Chiefs and the Otago Highlanders in next year's Super 12 rugby competition, NZPA reports.
While Cooper had been tipped to replace Brad Meurant, who quit at the end of a dismal 1997 campaign, Gilbert was a surprise pick.
He was Otago's NPC assistant coach in 1995 and was a Highlanders selector this year.

Among other names touted to replace Glenn Ross, who presided over a Highlanders side which finished bottom of the 1997 competition, were Canterbury Crusaders assistant coach Peter Sloane, former All Black Joe Stanley, current national selector -- and former Otago coach -- Gordon Hunter, and Auckland Blues and Auckland NPC coach Graham Henry.
Gilbert will be assisted by former South Canterbury coach Kevin Gloag, while Cooper's assistant will be New Zealand Maori coach Matt Te Pou.
Te Pou replaces Waikato coach John Boe, who was Meurant's assistant for the last two years.
Henry and Mac McCallion remain with the Auckland Blues, Frank Oliver and Graeme Taylor with the Wellington Hurricanes, and Wayne Smith and Sloane with Canterbury Crusaders.
Sloane had been earmarked for the Highlanders job, but convinced the New Zealand Rugby Football Union to leave him with Canterbury.
Cooper had been considered out of the running for the job as the New Zealand Rugby Football Union had earlier this year stipulated a Super 12 coach would be ineligible to be an All Black selector.
The unsuccessful candidates, like Boe, were not told of their fate until this morning, in some cases less than an hour before the official announcement.
All coaching appointments are for two years with the exception of Cooper, who has a one-year contract.
Cooper has been given "leave of absence" from the All Black selection panel for six months after the completion of the end-of-year tour to the United Kingdom.
When Cooper is finished with his Super 12 role at the end of May next year, he will rejoin the All Black selection panel up to and including the 1999 World Cup.
Hunter will retain his position as national selector through to the World Cup.
All Black coach, and selection panel convenor, John Hart, sees no problem in the NZRFU going against their own regulation imposed earlier this season.
He said their selection philosophy would remain intact.
"Gordon and I will carry on implementing the policies which the three of us have already put in place.
"We have maintained consistency throughout our time together. I am happy that this will continue, and we will welcome Ross back to the panel next June."
